relationships.subject: DkTx
relationships.evidence_quote: The spider venom protein, double-knot toxin (DkTx), partitions into the cellular membrane and binds bivalently to the pain-sensing ion channel, TRPV1, triggering long-lasting channel activation.

relationships.subject: SGTx
relationships.evidence_quote: The observation that appending a membrane partitioning moiety (SGTx) to the single-knots of DkTx slows down their wash-off rates establishes the important role of the membrane in endowing slow wash-off kinetics to DkTx

key_findings: Membrane affinity, together with bivalency, underlies the sustained TRPV1 activation by DkTx.
Tetra-knot toxins with higher membrane affinity give longer-lasting TRPV1 activation than DkTx.
